from_quote: is to consist of 65 members : that is, about one representative for fifty thousand inhabitants
rationale: Gives the House's 65 members, the total of the first apportionment, and says the legislature may increase the number "to one for each thirty thousand inhabitants," echoing this clause's "one for every thirty Thousand."

from_quote: to be chosen biennially
rationale: Says the House of Representatives is "to be chosen biennially," echoing this clause's "chosen every second Year."
to_quote: chosen every second Year

from_quote: Thirtythree representatives will make a quorum for doing business
rationale: Names the House quorum, "Thirtythree representatives," a majority of 65, echoing this clause's "Quorum to do Business."
to_quote: a Majority of each shall constitute a Quorum to do Business

from_quote: This, by a part of Art. i, Sect. 4, the general legislature may do, it may evidently so regulate elections
rationale: Cites "a part of Art. i, Sect. 4" (OCR "i" for "1") as letting the general legislature "regulate elections"; the part of that section on regulating elections is this clause.

from_quote: that part which authorises the congress to regulate elections
rationale: Continues the discussion of Art. 1, Sect. 4 begun in the previous paragraph, naming "that part which authorises the congress to regulate elections."

from_quote: The senate will consist of two members from each state, chosen by the state legislatures, every sixth year.
rationale: Describes the Senate as "two members from each state, chosen by the state legislatures, every sixth year," which only this clause provides.
to_quote: two Senators from each State, chosen by the Legislature thereof, for six Years

from_quote: except as to the places of chusing senators.
rationale: Quotes in quotation marks the clause's exception "except as to the places of chusing senators," referring back to "the clause referred to, respecting the elections of representatives."
to_quote: except as to the Places of chusing Senators

from_quote: Fourteen senators make a quorum for business
rationale: Names the Senate quorum, "Fourteen senators," a majority of 26, echoing this clause's "Quorum to do Business."
to_quote: a Majority of each shall constitute a Quorum to do Business

from_quote: except in giving judgment upon an impeachment
rationale: Names the requirement that "two-thirds of the senators present must agree" in "giving judgment upon an impeachment," which is in this clause.
to_quote: no Person shall be convicted without the Concurrence of two thirds of the Members present

from_quote: or in making treaties
rationale: Names the requirement that "two-thirds of the senators present must agree" "in making treaties," and the Senate's "negative in the making of all treaties, and in appointing almost all officers," both in this clause.
to_quote: provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: two-thirds of the members present, of either house, may expel a member
rationale: Says "two-thirds of the members present, of either house, may expel a member," echoing this clause's "with the Concurrence of two thirds, expel a Member."
to_quote: with the Concurrence of two thirds, expel a Member

from_quote: The members of the legislature are not excluded from being elected to any military offices, or any civil offices, except those created, or the emoluments of which shall be increased by themselves
rationale: Describes the exclusion of members from civil offices "created, or the emoluments of which shall be increased by themselves," which only this clause provides.
to_quote: which shall have been created, or the Emoluments whereof shall have been encreased during such time

from_quote: The vice president is not a very important, if not an unnecessary part of the system — he may be a part of the senate at one period
rationale: Says the vice president "may be a part of the senate," naming the provision that makes him President of the Senate, which is this clause.

from_quote: act as the supreme executive magistrate at another
rationale: Says the vice president may "act as the supreme executive magistrate," naming the provision for the President's powers to devolve on the Vice President, which is this clause.

from_quote: The president can appoint no officer, civil or military, who shall not be agreeable to the senate
rationale: Names the Senate's part in the President's appointments ("can appoint no officer ... who shall not be agreeable to the senate"), which is in this clause.
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, shall appoint

from_quote: the words authorizing the general government to regulate the elections of its own members
rationale: Names "the words authorizing the general government to regulate the elections of its own members," the clause the letter cited as Art. 1, Sect. 4 above.

from_quote: No judgment of conviction, on an impeachment, can be given unless two thirds of the senators agree.
rationale: Says officers are "impeachable before the senate only" and that no conviction can be given "unless two thirds of the senators agree," which is this clause.
to_quote: no Person shall be convicted without the Concurrence of two thirds of the Members present

from_quote: the right of impeachment, in the house
rationale: Names "the right of impeachment, in the house," the House's power of impeachment given in this clause.
to_quote: shall have the sole Power of Impeachment

from_quote: A power to lay and collect taxes at discretion
rationale: Names the proposed government's "power to lay and collect taxes," echoing this clause's "To lay and collect Taxes."
to_quote: To lay and collect Taxes

from_quote: to raise and support armies, but no appropriation of money to that use shall be for a longer term than two years
rationale: Quotes the clause verbatim in quotation marks, introduced as what "By the constitution it is proposed that congress shall have power" to do.
to_quote: To raise and support Armies, but no Appropriation of Money to that Use shall be for a longer Term than two Years

from_quote: to provide and maintain a navy
rationale: Quotes the clause verbatim within the quoted list of powers that "By the constitution it is proposed that congress shall have."
to_quote: To provide and maintain a Navy

from_quote: to provide for calling forth the militia to execute the laws of the union ; suppress insurrections, and repel invasions
rationale: Quotes the clause verbatim within the quoted list of powers that "By the constitution it is proposed that congress shall have."
to_quote: To provide for calling forth the Militia to execute the Laws of the Union, suppress Insurrections and repel Invasions

from_quote: to provide for organizing, arming, and disciplining the militia
rationale: Quotes the opening of the clause in quotation marks and goes on to paraphrase its reservation to the states of "the right to appoint the officers, and to train the militia according to the discipline prescribed by congress."
to_quote: To provide for organizing, arming, and disciplining, the Militia

from_quote: If uniform bankrupt laws can be made without producing real and substantial inconveniences, I wish them to be made by congress.
rationale: Discusses "general bankrupt laws, made by the union" and "uniform bankrupt laws" made by congress, echoing this clause's "uniform Laws on the subject of Bankruptcies."
to_quote: uniform Laws on the subject of Bankruptcies

from_quote: By Art. 3, Sec. 2. the powers of the federal judiciary are extended (among other things) to all cases between a state and citizens of another state — between citizens of different states — between a state or the citizens thereof, and foreign states, citizens or subjects.
rationale: Cites "Art. 3, Sec. 2" and quotes, without quotation marks, three of the clause's heads of jurisdiction, omitting the one on lands claimed under grants of different states.
to_quote: between a State and Citizens of another State,—between Citizens of different States,—between Citizens of the same State claiming Lands under Grants of different States, and between a State, or the Citizens thereof, and foreign States, Citizens or Subjects

from_quote: the supreme court shall have appellate jurisdiction, both as to law and fact, with such exception, and under such regulations as the congress shall make
rationale: Cites "Art. 3, Sec. 2" and reproduces this clause on original and appellate jurisdiction, nearly verbatim in its second sentence ("exception" for "Exceptions").
to_quote: the supreme Court shall have appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact, with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make

from_quote: a citizen may be tried for a crime committed in the state, and yet tried in some states 500 miles from the place where it was committed
rationale: Says jury trial "is secured only in those few criminal cases" and that a crime is to be tried in the state where it was committed, which together only this clause provides.
to_quote: such Trial shall be held in the State where the said Crimes shall have been committed

from_quote: except paper money and tender laws, which are wisely guarded against in the proposed constitution
rationale: Names the proposed constitution's guard against state "paper money and tender laws," the bars on emitting bills of credit and on tenders in this clause.

from_quote: The judicial powers of the federal courts extend in law and equity to certain cases
rationale: Says the judicial powers "extend in law and equity to certain cases," echoing this clause's "shall extend to all Cases, in Law and Equity."
to_quote: The judicial Power shall extend to all Cases, in Law and Equity

from_quote: This court is to have appellate jurisdiction in all the other cases before mentioned
rationale: Repeats this clause's words "appellate jurisdiction in all the other cases before mentioned" without quotation marks.
to_quote: In all the other Cases before mentioned, the supreme Court shall have appellate Jurisdiction

from_quote: How far it may be proper to admit a foreigner or the citizen of another state to bring actions against state governments
rationale: Discusses the new jurisdiction allowing "a foreigner or the citizen of another state to bring actions against state governments," the heads of jurisdiction in this clause cited in FederalFarmer.3.20.
